title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 38
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's sickness, the fifteen added years, the sign of the sundial and his song of recovery.

questions.text: What message did Isaiah bring to Hezekiah when he was sick and near death?
questions.explanation: Isaiah told him that Yahweh said, "Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live."

answers.text: "Be strong, for you will recover in three days."
"Flee the city, for Assyria is coming."
"Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live."
"Appoint your son king in your place."

questions.text: What did Hezekiah do when he heard that he would die?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, prayed to Yahweh, and wept bitterly.

answers.text: He turned his face to the wall, prayed, and wept bitterly
He called for his sons and blessed them
He put on royal robes and sat on his throne
He sent messengers to the temple with offerings

questions.text: How many years did Yahweh say he would add to Hezekiah's life?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life."

answers.text: Ten years
Seven years
Forty years
Fifteen years

questions.text: What was the sign that Yahweh would do what he had spoken?
questions.explanation: Yahweh caused the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz to return backward ten steps.

answers.text: The sun stood still in the sky for a whole day
The shadow on the sundial of Ahaz returned backward ten steps
A new star appeared in the heavens at noon
Rain fell on the land at the time of the wheat harvest

questions.text: What is the passage beginning in verse 9 said to be?
questions.explanation: It is the writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick and had recovered of his sickness.

answers.text: A psalm of David to be sung by the sick
A letter sent by Isaiah to the king of Judah
The writing of Hezekiah when he had been sick and recovered
A prayer offered by the priests in the temple

questions.text: In his writing, Hezekiah says he has rolled up his life like whom?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah says, "I have rolled up my life like a weaver. He will cut me off from the loom."

answers.text: A fisherman
A harvester
A potter
A weaver

questions.text: Like which birds did Hezekiah say he chattered and moaned?
questions.explanation: He says, "I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove."

answers.text: Like a swallow or a crane, and moaned like a dove
Like a sparrow and an eagle of the mountains
Like a raven and an owl of the desert
Like an ostrich and a stork of the heavens

questions.text: What does Hezekiah say God has cast behind his back?
questions.explanation: He says that in love God delivered his soul from the pit of corruption and cast all his sins behind his back.

answers.text: All my enemies
All my sins
All my tears
All my riches

questions.text: According to Hezekiah, who shall praise Yahweh?
questions.explanation: He says that Sheol cannot praise God and death cannot celebrate him, but the living, the living shall praise him.

answers.text: Those who go down into the pit
The angels in heaven
The kings of the earth
The living

questions.text: What did Isaiah say should be laid as a poultice on the boil?
questions.explanation: Isaiah had said, "Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall recover."

answers.text: A cake of figs
Olive oil and wine
A bronze serpent
Crushed herbs and honey
